etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English abundaunce, habaundance, from Old French habundance, abondance, from Latin abundantia (“fullness, plenty”), from abundō (“to overflow”). Equivalent to abound +‎ -ance. Displaced Old English geniht (“abundance, plenty”).

definitions.definition: A large quantity; many. [First attested around 1150 to 1350.][2]
An overflowing fullness or ample sufficiency; profusion; copious supply; superfluity; plentifulness. [First attested around 1350 to 1470.][2]

quote.citation: c. 1610?, Walter Raleigh, A Discourse of War:
quote.text: It is lamentable to remember what abundance of noble blood hath been shed with small benefit to the Christian state.

definitions.definition: Wealth; affluence; plentiful amount of resources. [First attested around 1350 to 1470.][2]
Frequency, amount, ratio of something within a given environment or sample. [First attested in the late 19th century.][2]
(card games) A bid to take nine or more tricks in solo whist. [First attested in the late 19th century.][2]
